Back to the part where we talk about the timing chip in your mouth 😂

When you take your wetsuit off you have to take your timing chip off first and it’s really easy to throw it on the ground… and forget about it.

Without it you don’t get recorded or get a finish time… so lots of people put it in their mouth whilst they take off their wetsuit, then put it STRAIGHT BACK ON.

It’s a good way to ensure you don’t forget about it!!!!

IS IT HARD TO FINISH AN IRONMAN?
My honest answer?
No.
It’s actually pretty easy to cross that finish line.
Because by the time you get there, the hard part has already been done.
The hard part is the hours and hours of training in the rain, the cold and the heatwave.
It’s training when you have zero motivation.
It’s the sacrifices away from friends and family.
It’s 9 months of 4–6 hour bike rides on Saturdays and long runs every Sunday.
It’s the early nights in bed while everyone else is out, knowing you have another big training day waiting for you in the morning.
It’s the constant battle in your own head convincing yourself, again and again, that you are capable.
There were days when I questioned myself. Days when I got knocked down. But somehow, I kept getting back up.
Because becoming an Ironman isn’t just about swimming 3.8km, cycling 180km and running a marathon.
It’s about who you have to become to get to that start line.
So when I finally crossed that finish line and heard those four words…
YOU ARE AN IRONMAN.
There really are no words to describe that feeling.
9 months of sacrifice.
9 months of discipline.
9 months of believing.
And in that moment, it was all worth it.
I AM AN IRONMAN. 🦾🔥

Wow Ironman Leeds what can I say? You kicked my arse… both mentally and physically 😂 

By cancelling the swim late you really disrupted my focus going into the day (no question about the decision though as the lake was minging) and by god you do love a hill don’t you? 

Started off strong on my road bike (yes road bike, not TT… I’m a traditional fella 😃) but before today my furthest ride was 100K… by the time I hit 120K my legs really started to feel it and started cramping up. 

I must say that the people of Leeds did not disappoint! The crowds at the top of Black Hill Road were electric, reminiscent of Alpe d’Huez In the Tour de France. Their amazing support somehow managed to carry me up that monster of a hill 3 times 🙌  The crowds everywhere were great but especially in Thorner, absolutely loved riding through this beautiful village with some really incredible people who were standing outside for hours cheering us on! 🙌

Started the run off strong but Leeds does love a good hill and by the end I couldn’t ingest anymore gels and was running on fumes… decided to rein it in the last two laps and soak up the amazing atmosphere!

Yes I rang the bell… I know people may have an issue with that but that’s your problem 😝 I can only race what’s in front of me and wanted to embrace the full experience as I may never do one of these again. 

Whilst I know it doesn’t count, in my OCD brain it does, I did the 3.8K swim today in the local pool 😂

IRONMAN UK LEEDS 🚴‍♂️🏃‍♂️

Leading the race, feeling great… then a completely flat rear tyre. 🤦‍♂️

A strange day from the start with the swim cancelled. Whether you’re a good swimmer or not, nobody wants that, especially the first-timers who’d trained for the full Ironman experience.

The bike started in a TT format. I felt good, took the lead early and managed to pull out a decent gap. Having the lead car in front was a great feeling what I hadn’t had for a while. 

Then my rear tyre started bottoming out, exactly like in Lanzarote only a lot earlier.I hoped it was in my head, but it soon became obvious I was riding on a completely flat tyre.

I rode for around 15 minutes out of the saddle trying to make it to Black Hill. Getting up there on a flat was brutal!

The support at the top was incredible. So many people tried to help, some even putting their own races on hold. Two guys from Total Tri went above and beyond to get me going again. 🙏

28 minutes lost, quads seized, but back in the race.

By the last bike lap my legs had pretty much packed up and I seriously considered calling it a day.

Then I saw my family cheering like I was still leading ❤️ and heard Abbey shout. Straight away I thought of @Kieran and what he’d be saying…

“Stop being a soft lad!” 🤦‍♂️🤣

Decision made. I was finishing.

After surgery and a soleus tear this year I’d missed a lot of running, but surprisingly I felt OK and was told I was 3rd in my AG. Maybe Kona was still on…

Mixed feelings reflecting on my 16th full-distance IRONMAN at IRONMAN Leeds! 🏊‍♂️🚫🇬🇧
Every finish line teaches you something new, but this one hit differently. Standing on the edge of the water only to have the swim cancelled (check out the picture—nature definitely had the final say!) immediately threw off the usual race-day rhythm.
On top of that, transitioning straight from weeks of grinding through intense summer heat back home in Switzerland to the classic, unpredictable UK conditions was a whole separate mind game. The legs held up and the grit was there, but it’s a strong reminder that no two 140.6 races are ever the same—even when you’ve done 16 of them.
Grateful for another medal, another story, and the incredible support along the course. Time to recover and process it all! 🏁🚴‍♂️🏃‍♂️

💙💛🏊🏻🚴🏻🏃🏻The curse of Leeds Ironman for our very own Jamie Heselden.

Rewind to July 2025, Leeds first Ironman and Jamie was off to a good start finishing the swim in 1 hour 26 minutes. The discipline he’d been dreading the most and yet he’d managed to master giving himself a good 50 minute buffer for the bike. 

Only just a few miles into the bike he realised the gears on the bike weren’t switching into higher gears making it impossible to cycle the hilly course. Despite course mechanics attempting to help out Jamie’s Ironman dreams came to an end at just 18 miles and after hours of waiting and trying to fix it. DNF.

Fast forward to 2026 another years worth of training under the belt and less than 24 hours prior to the event the swim is cancelled due to blue green algae. 

While he’ll begin the bike start at 7am with all the other Ironman athletes we can’t help but wonder will Jamie ever complete the full Leeds Ironman? 🤔

Not an Ironman but a Tinman!

IRONMAN Leeds: The Bike 🚲

The bike lived up to all expectations and then some. 

At 180 km with ~2600 m elevation this was no joke.

I decided to take the road bike instead of the TT bike. Choosing to take an aluminium frame and no aero bars I knew I was going to be slower than I could have been, but the goal was to simply save the legs (my nemesis, the hip flexors) for my first marathon and I am glad I did. Some of those descents were so gnarly I don't think my TT bike brake pads would have survived anyway 😂

Pushing on to Black Hill - 3 repeats of this climb reaching 19% gradient in parts - with spectators lining the most brutal part was awesome! @blackhill_wrestlers_imuk doing what they do best and motivating us up 🦸🦹💪 managed to pedal up all three times which I was happy with, but was probably hitting 15 RPM and 180 BPM on the last climb 🗻

I managed to get a puncture at 80K which was demoralising.  In the back wheel too - flipped the bike and lost 50% of my water in the process. Changed the tube and got some help from a handy Moto official who had a digital pump to top the Psi back up to 65. Overall lost 21 mins on the bike which is a long time to change a tube. A lesson in composure was learned. Got back on and legs were seized up from being stationary, got in my head a bit after seeing so many people fly by, but got my head back in the game anyway. 

Rocked into T2 after 7 hours and got through transition quite quickly in 5 mins considering my bike was basically the f

Who knew swimming 3.8km, cycling 180km and running a marathon could be so addictive? 🧐

The bike was super tough with 2700m elevation including the perilous Black Hill climb which we got to do 3 times 🙃 dropping my chain, getting a puncture and having to fix my hydration system while out on course didn’t help either. 
As expected the marathon was hard, but my head stayed in the game and we managed to cross that finish line to become an Ironman. 

Awesome experience. Would do it again. 

Thanks everyone for your support 🙏🏻 especially those that trained with me, coached me and put up with the gruelling training schedule 😁
